name: HeLa USD
oneLiner: HLUSD is the HeLa ecosystem's centralized dollar stablecoin, backed by fiat and fiat-equivalent reserves and used as the HeLa runtime settlement asset.
collateral: Off-chain USDC reserves held with a licensed financial institution in Australia, backing HLUSD redeemable 1:1 for the U.S. dollar
pegMechanism: Fiat-collateralized 1:1 USD peg: HLUSD is minted against off-chain USDC reserves and redeemable at 1 HLUSD = 1 USD, with issuance and redemption controlled by HeLa's on-chain role-based mint/burn governance (MintProposer/MintVoter quorum and Admin). HLUSD also serves as HeLa Chain's native gas token. Pricing and market-cap coverage are sourced from CoinGecko because the native HeLa chain is not modeled in Pharos.

mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: HeLa's official May 7, 2024 mainnet launch notice identifies HLUSD as the network's native stablecoin in live use. HeLa's HLUSD documentation describes 1:1 backing by custodial USDC and redemption at the dollar, supporting the fiat-cash archetype for this implementation.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: 2026-07-30 re-read of HeLa stablecoin-governance docs: BlacklistProposer/BlacklistVoter roles submit and vote blacklist proposals; when blacklistQuorum is reached the target becomes BlacklistedUser and cannot send any transactions that change that runtime's state (including queries). The HeLa whitepaper §6.2 independently lists blacklist among the six on-chain stablecoin actions under the same role/quorum model. Scope is runtime-native HLUSD on HeLa Official Runtime (chain id 8668, mainnet-rpc.helachain.com); CoinGecko lists no external-platform contract, and Pharos has no modeled EVM token surface. No separate global transfer-pause or rate-limit control is published; holder-level freeze/censor is the blacklist path. Failure domain: protocol:hela-runtime-stablecoin-governance.

mintAuthority.summary: HLUSD issuance is controlled by HeLa's on-chain governance roles: MintProposer initiates mint requests, MintVoter approval satisfies the configured quorum, and Admin configures role/quorum parameters.

controls.label: HeLa MintProposer/MintVoter quorum
controls.evidence: HeLa governance docs define HLUSD minting as a chain-runtime quorum action: MintProposer addresses propose mints to whitelisted users and MintVoter addresses approve until mintQuorum is reached; proposals and votes execute inside the HeLa runtime (not an EVM contract). The HeLa mainnet EVM gateway (mainnet-rpc.helachain.com, chain id 8668) is live, but the native role state is exposed only through the HeLa runtime API/CLI (hela managest), so individual role-holder addresses remain unenumerated through standard JSON-RPC.

controls.label: HeLa Admin role
controls.evidence: HeLa governance docs state the Admin role proposes and votes on all other roles and configures mintQuorum, burnQuorum, whitelistQuorum, blacklistQuorum, and configQuorum within the HeLa runtime's on-chain proposal system; the initial Chain Initiator assignment is single-use and afterwards all role management flows through propose-vote governance.

controls.label: HeLa runtime upgrade authority (unresolved)
controls.evidence: 2026-08-08 re-check: HeLa stablecoin-governance docs still define only mint/burn/whitelist/blacklist/config/setroles actions and publish neither a runtime bytecode-upgrade executor nor its threshold or delay. Architecture documentation confirms that execution layers can be upgraded independently, while tokenomics only says $HELA holders may participate in protocol upgrades. The live public gateway returned chain id 8668 and block 660832, but standard JSON-RPC exposes no runtime role or upgrade-admin state. The authority model therefore remains issuer-undisclosed rather than guessed.

review.evidence: The documented model is clear but the live controller inventory is not: MintProposer/MintVoter may propose and approve arbitrary mint amounts to whitelisted users once mintQuorum is reached, and Admin governs the role/quorum configuration. No numeric supply cap is documented, so economic cap semantics remain unbounded; as a runtime-governed native asset, reserve reconciliation is not applicable. On 2026-08-08 the official EVM gateway was live at chain id 8668 and block 660832, but it exposes neither the runtime-native role roster/current quorum values nor the runtime code-upgrade authority. Current governance, architecture, endpoint, tokenomics, whitepaper, explorer, and public repository review still identify no upgrade executor, threshold, or timelock. The review is therefore explicitly unresolved rather than scoreable.
review.sourceFreeRationale: Classification based on the role-based mint governance model in HeLa documentation; the on-chain role holder addresses could not be resolved because HLUSD's native HeLa chain is not modeled in Pharos contracts.
unresolvedQuestions: What are the current MintProposer, MintVoter, and Admin holder addresses and configured quorum values on the HeLa runtime?
Which address or governance executor can upgrade the HLUSD runtime logic, and what threshold and delay govern that action?

notices.title: Native chain not yet supported
notices.message: CoinGecko lists HLUSD without a supported Pharos contract platform. Runtime coverage uses the CoinGecko price and market-cap path while contract coverage remains intentionally absent.
